The arc melting method was used to form the button-shaped cast ingots. To ensure homogeneous melting and avoid segregation, samples were flipped and remelted 6 times during the melting process.
Each sample was cut from the cast ingots and was sealed into a quartz tube with Ar gas. Those were homogenized at 1273 K for 7.2 ks.
After homogenization heat treatments, all alloys formed a β-BCC single phase matrix, and aging treatment formed α-HCP precipitates distributed.

The aging treatment was also conducted at different temperature for 86.4ks. The aging temperatures of each alloy were as follows; 873 K for Alloy A, 750 K for Alloy B, 850 K for Alloy C, 973 K for Alloy D and Alloy E. All of the samples were cooled down by quenching in the water.

conflicts.description: The paper states that Ti3Al formation contributes to high strength in Alloys D and E, but also states that Ti3Al was not detected in XRD patterns.
conflicting_claims: Another aspect contributing to the high strength at high temperatures in Alloys D and E is the formation of Ti3Al, which occurs due to the high Al content exceeding 10 at%.
However, Ti3Al was not detected in the XRD patterns (Fig. 4).
